title: A Metric for HPC Programming Model Productivity
problem: Selecting appropriate HPC programming models is challenging because productivity metrics are reduced to basic measures like SLOC. Developers lack objective methods to compare productivity across diverse heterogeneous programming paradigms.
motivation: As HPC systems become increasingly heterogeneous with multiple programming models, developers need objective productivity metrics to guide technology selection and performance-productivity tradeoff analysis.
method: The paper introduces a model divergence measure that quantifies programming model productivity by analyzing syntax, semantics, and optimization overhead. A framework supporting GCC and Clang compilers was built for C/C++ and Fortran analysis. The metric was validated on SPEChpc miniapps and other benchmarks, with results presented as combined productivity-performance probability visualizations.
key_novelty: A novel model divergence measure that objectively quantifies HPC programming model productivity beyond simple source lines of code.
contributions: Model divergence measure for objective productivity evaluation of heterogeneous HPC programming models
Productivity analysis framework supporting GCC, Clang, C/C++, and Fortran
Comprehensive evaluation methodology on SPEChpc miniapps and benchmarks
Combined productivity-performance probability visualization for integrated model comparison
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in abstract.
